_note: Holdout program. Deliberately a different domain, a different shape (3 hypotheses, 8 assumptions, 9 experiments, heavier ESTABLISHES fan-out), and different wording from the ARC program, so a system that learned the first program's phrasing gets no help here. Synthetic but realistic; every excerpt occurs verbatim in the source it names.

questions.text: Does typed compression of tool results preserve enough signal for long-horizon coding agents to finish tasks that exceed the context budget?

hypotheses.question: RQ2
hypotheses.text: Typed compression of tool results preserves task-relevant signal better than fixed-window truncation at an equal token budget.

hypotheses.question: RQ2
hypotheses.text: Most of the gain from compression comes from collapsing duplicate observations rather than from summary quality.

hypotheses.question: RQ2
hypotheses.text: Compression failures concentrate in tasks that require exact string recall from an earlier tool result.

assumptions.text: Agent trajectories in this benchmark exceed the context budget on at least 40% of tasks, so compression is worth doing at all.
Fixed-window truncation drops task-critical observations at a measurable rate rather than only redundant ones.
Duplicate observations account for a large share of trajectory tokens.
Tasks requiring exact string recall form a distinguishable subset that can be labelled reliably.
The benchmark's grader is deterministic, so a task's pass or fail is not run-to-run noise.
A typed summary can be produced inside the agent loop's per-step latency budget.
Context window length, not attention degradation over long inputs, is the binding constraint on these tasks.
The benchmark's task distribution resembles the deployment distribution closely enough to generalise.

experiments.text: Trajectory length audit across 600 benchmark tasks.
Duplicate observation analysis over the same trajectories.
Failed: free-text LLM summarisation at a 4k budget, no gain over truncation.
Typed compression against fixed-window truncation at four token budgets.
Duplicate-removal ablation: dedupe only, no summarisation.
Exact-recall subset study: label the subset, then measure failure concentration.
Grader reliability re-run: 50 tasks, five repeats each.
Per-step latency measurement for typed summary generation.
Attention degradation probe: fixed length, varying distractor density.

sources.title: F1 trajectory audit, 2026-06-02
sources.text: Of 600 tasks, 317 produced trajectories longer than the 128k context budget before the agent halted. Median overflow was 41k tokens. The longest 5% of trajectories were dominated by repeated file reads.

sources.title: F2 duplicate observation analysis, 2026-06-20
sources.text: Exact-duplicate tool results accounted for 38% of trajectory tokens across the corpus, and near-duplicates a further 14%. Removing exact duplicates alone brought 122 of the 317 overflowing trajectories back inside budget.

sources.title: F3 negative result, 2026-07-08
sources.text: Free-text summarisation at a 4k budget matched truncation to within 0.4 points of task success. Inspecting failures, the summaries dropped exact identifiers such as file paths and error codes that later steps needed verbatim.

sources.title: Harness review, 2026-05-18
sources.text: The grader compares process exit status and a canonical diff, with no model in the loop. Repeated runs of the same trajectory produced identical verdicts on all 40 spot-checked tasks.

claims.text: More than half of tasks overflow the budget.
